what_its_for: Irbesartan is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). Lowering blood pressure helps prevent strokes, heart attacks, and kidney problems. It is also used to protect the kidneys in people with type 2 diabetes who have high blood pressure.
how_to_take: Take irbesartan by mouth, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time every day so it becomes part of your routine. Do not stop taking this medicine on your own, even if you feel fine — high blood pressure often has no symptoms.
dosing: The usual starting dose for adults is 150 mg once daily. Your doctor may increase your dose to 300 mg once daily if needed. For kidney protection in diabetic patients, the target dose is usually 300 mg once daily. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and just take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at once to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store irbesartan at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid potassium supplements or salt substitutes containing potassium unless your doctor tells you it is okay — irbesartan can raise potassium levels in your blood. Avoid NSAIDs (like ibuprofen or naproxen) without checking with your doctor, as they can reduce the effectiveness of irbesartan and harm your kidneys. Limit alcohol, as it can lower your blood pressure too much and cause dizziness. Avoid becoming dehydrated — drink enough fluids, especially in hot weather or during exercise.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat (signs of a serious allergic reaction called angioedema); dizziness or fainting; signs of high potassium such as muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat, or numbness; decreased urination or signs of kidney problems; or if you become pregnant, since irbesartan can harm an unborn baby and must be stopped immediately during pregnancy.
when_it_works: Irbesartan begins to lower your blood pressure within 1 to 2 hours after your first dose. However, it may take 4 to 6 weeks of regular use before you get the full benefit. Keep taking it as prescribed even if you feel well.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do NOT use irbesartan if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby. Use reliable birth control while taking this medicine and tell your doctor immediately if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding: It is not known if irbesartan passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: Irbesartan is not recommended for children under 18 years old. Elderly: Older adults may be more sensitive to the blood pressure-lowering effects and dizziness. Rise slowly from sitting or lying down to reduce the risk of falls. Kidney or Liver Problems: Your doctor may adjust your dose if you have severe kidney or liver disease.
